objective: Demonstrate understanding of different data formats and types by recognizing each file type and assessing its validity. Data formats to include FASTA, FASTQ, BED, BEDPE, WIG, GTF/GFF3, SAM, BAM, CRAM, gVCF, VCF, and GFA.
scope_note: Introductory operational recognition and justified validity assessment for all 13 named formats, with GTF and GFF3 as distinct targets. Teach necessary sequence, read/reference, record, coordinate, quality, feature, alignment, allele, graph and container foundations. Conditions always state excerpt versus complete file, version/producer profile, supplied lookup keys, available reference context and tool-report scope. Main examples use genomic DNA FASTA while recognizing protein FASTA; modern unwrapped Phred+33 FASTQ with wrapping/encoding boundaries; GA4GH BEDv1 and explicit consumer differences; bedtools BEDPE; both UCSC WIG modes; Ensembl-style GTF; GFF3 specification 1.26; SAM/BAM1.6; CRAM3.0/3.1; version-declared simple VCF; common GATK VCF4.2 <NON_REF>/END gVCF with newer VCF4.5 representation boundaries; GFA1.0 H/S/L/P with later-version boundaries. Complex permitted constructs are identified as documentation/context cases, not incorrectly rejected by a simplified rule. This route does not require programming, alignment algorithms, probability/logarithm derivations, a full analysis pipeline or memorization of every specification field. Selecting/interpreting bounded checks is in scope; executing production validators and establishing biological correctness of unknown files require additional evidence. Required edges describe the component operations of this chosen instructional route, not measured learner mastery or an empirically validated KST space.

items.label: Read structured records
items.capability: Given a field key and a labeled text example, distinguish headers from data, split records using the stated delimiter, identify named fields and identifiers, and distinguish a missing-value marker from an empty or malformed field.
items.entry_reason: Instruction introduces a record as one structured entry and a header as its key using familiar labeled lists; only reading and counting are assumed.

items.label: Sequence letters and orientation
items.capability: Given a declared molecule/alphabet profile and supplied ambiguity/complement key, count sequence symbols, interpret A/C/G/T and N in DNA, distinguish nucleotide from protein examples, and find the reverse complement of a short DNA sequence.
items.entry_reason: Instruction introduces sequences as ordered letters and provides the complement key; reading, reversal of a short list, and counting use the baseline.
items.notes: An alphabet-compatible short string does not uniquely determine DNA versus protein. Use the declared profile; N denotes an ambiguous nucleotide, not an absent tabular value.

source_refs.locator: Definition-line guidance and Sample Protein FASTA

items.label: Text, compression and indexes
items.capability: Given a labeled storage/decoding description, distinguish plain sequence or tabular text, compressed text, binary alignment containers and indexes; explain why a filename, magic bytes, decoded preview or index establishes only the stated kind of evidence.
items.entry_reason: Instruction introduces storage, decoding and indexes with a document/container analogy; no programming, compression algorithm or command-line experience is assumed.

items.label: Scope a validity judgment
items.capability: Given a stated version/profile and an excerpt, complete fixture or check report, separate record-level violations, whole-file consistency/decoding, reference or producer context, and consumer policy; conclude 'violation found', 'passes the stated checks', or 'insufficient evidence' with the missing evidence named.
items.entry_reason: Instruction first contrasts checking one entry with checking a whole document and with checking its claims; later format branches supply the domain-specific rules.
items.notes: The three conclusions describe available evidence. A passed parser or scoped validator does not prove biological correctness; command examples are guidance unless an actual execution report is supplied.

items.label: Positioned numeric signals
items.capability: Given a declaration and short numeric series, distinguish positions from measured values, compute successive positions using start and step, apply span as a count, and distinguish an omitted measurement from zero.
items.entry_reason: The sequence is a familiar table of positions and numbers; supplied start/step/span definitions require only counting and basic arithmetic.

items.label: Reads and named references
items.capability: Given a small sequencing example, distinguish a read from a reference sequence, identify the named sequence on which a position is defined, and explain why reference/assembly identity and supplied length are needed for contextual checks.

source_refs.locator: Definition sections: DNA Sequencing, Human Genome Reference Sequence, Chromosome

items.label: Coordinate conventions
items.capability: Given a named reference and an explicitly stated convention, locate a feature using zero-based half-open or one-based inclusive coordinates, calculate covered length, convert an ordinary nonempty interval between conventions, and distinguish a bounds violation from unavailable reference-length evidence.
items.notes: Ordinary interval conversions are the starting route. Zero-length BED sites, unknown BEDPE sentinels and circular or telomeric exceptions require their explicitly declared format rules.

items.label: Quality values and their referents
items.capability: Given a declared Phred offset and character-value table, decode per-base quality characters, match one character to each base, distinguish base quality from mapping and variant/genotype confidence, and identify unavailable quality rather than treating it as maximal confidence.
items.notes: Use lookup and subtraction with an explicit encoding key; logarithms and probability derivations are not prerequisites. Low confidence is a data-quality issue, not by itself malformed serialization.

items.label: Annotation features and relationships
items.capability: Given a small labeled gene model and feature key, distinguish gene, transcript, exon and CDS, follow a feature's parent relationship, and identify the strand-relative 5′ end used by a supplied CDS-phase rule; explain why an exon need not be wholly protein-coding.

items.label: Read alignment consistency
items.capability: Given a mapped or unmapped read example with a FLAG/CIGAR key, identify read/reference roles, interpret the selected flag and missing markers, sum query- and reference-consuming CIGAR operations, check sequence/quality lengths, and relate an ordinary mapped span to its reference position.
items.notes: The key supplies bit meanings and operation consumption; binary arithmetic and alignment algorithms are not assumed. M does not distinguish a match from a mismatch; unmapped and unavailable-field cases use their stated rules.

items.label: Alleles and genotype indexes
items.capability: Given a reference/alternate allele list and a genotype key, identify REF and each ALT, decode indexes 0/1/2 and phased/unphased separators, distinguish missing alleles from homozygous reference, and state what exact-reference evidence would establish REF agreement.
items.notes: Initial examples use simple substitutions and explicitly stated ploidy; diploidy is not a rule for every sample or locus.

research_gaps.question: Which elementary biological definitions must be taught before a novice can interpret sequences, references, annotation features and genotype indexes?
research_gaps.why_needed: Backward mapping exposed unexplained DNA/protein, read/reference, exon/CDS and allele/genotype terms. Resolved through the added NHGRI Definition entries, Ensembl transcript/CDS tutorial and NCBI protein FASTA example; their passages are anchored on the affected items.
research_gaps.depth: Only terminology and short sequence/feature examples needed by the target checks; no complete genetics or sequencing course.

research_gaps.question: Which coordinate conventions, unknown sentinels and exceptional cases would make a single generic interval rule unsafe?
research_gaps.why_needed: The formats mix half-open and inclusive coordinates, BED insertion sites, BEDPE unknown sentinels and circular/telomeric exceptions. The inspected definitions resolve which ordinary checks can be taught and which need a declared exception/profile rather than automatic rejection.
research_gaps.depth: Ordinary interval location/length/conversion, reference bounds and recognition of documented exception cases.

research_gaps.question: What evidence distinguishes binary-format recognition, scoped integrity checks, full restoration and contextual or semantic validity?
research_gaps.why_needed: A binary preview, index or quickcheck cannot support the whole objective. SAM/BAM and CRAM definitions plus samtools/Picard guidance distinguish signatures, skipped middle records, full decoding, stricter policy and required versus embedded/reference-free resources.
research_gaps.depth: Read and interpret supplied versioned check reports; no compression internals or unexecuted production-validation claims.

research_gaps.question: Which producer/version differences must be explicit to avoid classifying unsupported or alternative legal files as intrinsically invalid?
research_gaps.why_needed: Primary specifications and producer manuals resolve FASTQ encoding/wrapping, BED parser policy, GTF feature-dependent attributes, GATK versus current-VCF gVCF conventions and GFA additions. The chosen profiles preserve every requested format while keeping each validity decision bounded.
research_gaps.depth: Teach the common stated profiles and identify when documentation or producer metadata is required; do not claim one universal parser or silently apply the latest grammar to older declarations.

alternative_routes: Documentation remains available for field, encoding, FLAG/CIGAR, phase and validator keys. A competent learner may use the originals while applying the checks; required edges concern understanding the component operations rather than recalling tables from memory (s003 Table 1; s011 §1.4; s010 Column 8; s015 quickcheck/view descriptions).

GATK's BP_RESOLUTION gVCF is a valid producer route without multi-base END blocks; current VCF4.5 REF-only block syntax is another explicitly versioned representation. Neither route is an additional prerequisite to the common GATK VCF4.2 branch (s014 Types of GVCFs and example records; s013 §5.5).

FASTA and FASTQ, SAM/BAM/CRAM, and VCF/gVCF share foundations but remain parallel target capabilities. Their specifications expose common components; they do not establish an obligatory sequence of format courses (s001 FASTA/FASTQ Files; s011 §§1.4 and 4; s012 §11; s013 §§1.6 and 5.5; s014 introductory sections).
